title: Authentication scheme
description: How a secret value is set on a request, from the closed set of schemes the proxy implements. bearer sets Authorization: Bearer and the value. header sets the header in header to the value. basic sets Authorization: Basic with the username in username and the value as the password. oauth, only with bearer, marks the value as an OAuth token, such as a Claude subscription login's: the proxy sets it as any bearer, and the session reads it to choose the runtime's variable for a model key. account_header and account_claim, both or neither and only with oauth, make the proxy read a claim of the value's JWT payload and set it in a header beside the value, for a model API that needs the subscription's account id on every request.

account_header.description: The HTTP header the proxy sets to the value of account_claim on every request it sets the value on, such as chatgpt-account-id. A header that frames the request, is hop-by-hop or that the proxy sets is run_configuration_invalid: Authorization, Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Connection, TE, Trailer, Upgrade, Keep-Alive, Expect, Cookie, and any header that starts with Proxy-, X-Qory- or Qory-, with case ignored and an underscore read as a dash, the headers of server.ReservedHeader and Authorization.

account_claim.description: Where the header's value lies in the payload of the value, a JWT: a JSON pointer, RFC 6901, into the payload's JSON object, with ~1 for / and ~0 for ~ inside a member name, such as /https:~1~1api.openai.com~1auth/chatgpt_account_id. The member it points at is a string.

reserved_header.description: The headers account_header may not be: those server.ReservedHeader reports, and Authorization, in any letter case and with _ in place of -.
